title: Finding Report
description: The report format every OPF tool shares. A finding is one thing a checker found at one place in a presentation: a stable rule id, a severity, a category, a JSON Pointer path, a message, and optionally source positions, the measured numbers behind it and suggested fixes as JSON Patch. `validate` in `@openpresentation/opf`, the Markdown and YAML converters, the editor's Review panel and hosted reviewers such as pptx.dev's AI review all produce this shape, so a host shows and applies findings from any of them the same way. A report lists findings, tells whether any has severity `error` (`valid`) and counts them by severity; `validate` adds `schemaValid`, `checks` and variable fields on top of it. Core's checks are deterministic and run locally; findings from other producers use their own rule-id prefix and say so in `source`.

valid.description: True when no finding has severity `error`.

counts.description: How many findings each severity has.

FindingSeverity.description: `error` makes a report invalid. `warning` is a problem the author should fix. `info` is advisory.

FindingCategory.description: What kind of question the finding answers. Core uses `format` (is it well-formed OPF), `references` (does everything it points at resolve), `policy` (host house rules), `accessibility`, `layout` (will it present as authored) and `content` (is anything left unfinished). Other producers may use their own category names, such as `narrative` or `audience-fit`.

FindingLocation.description: A range in the checked text: UTF-16 offset and length from the start, and the one-based line and column of the start. Present when the finding was produced from text (JSON, Markdown or YAML).

JsonPatchOperation.description: One RFC 6902 JSON Patch operation. Paths are JSON Pointers into the checked presentation.

FindingFocus.description: The field an author has to fill in, for a fix that cannot be written as a patch.

path.description: JSON Pointer of the field to edit.

field.description: What the field is, such as `alt`, `title`, `text`, `link`, `language` or `fontSize`.

value.description: The field's current value, when it has one.

FindingFix.description: A suggested repair. Core never applies it: the host shows it and applies it through its own undoable edit path. A `patch` fix carries JSON Patch operations; a `focus` fix only names the field the author has to fill in.

title.description: What applying the fix does, in a few words.

id.description: Stable id within one finding, such as `focus-alt` or `use-readable-color`.

safe.description: True when applying the fix cannot change what the content says or how it looks beyond the repair, such as switching a failing colour to the one the theme chose. False fixes need a deliberate choice.

patch.description: RFC 6902 JSON Patch operations that apply the fix to the checked presentation.

FindingSuggestion.description: A value the author could use instead, such as a catalog record that exists. Suggestions name records actually present in the checked context and never replace authored values silently.

origin.description: Where the suggestion comes from: `schema`, `built-in`, `loaded`, `document` or `contract`.

definition.description: Where the suggested record or constraint is defined.

ValidationIssue.description: The raw schema or semantic issue behind a finding, kept with every union alternative so a host can inspect the exact constraint.

keyword.description: The JSON Schema keyword that failed, or `opf` for a rule the schema cannot express.

Finding.description: One thing a checker found at one place in a presentation.

ruleId.description: Stable `<producer>/<rule>` id, such as `opf/text-contrast` for core or `pptx.dev/narrative-gap` for a hosted reviewer. Ids do not change between releases.

source.description: The producer: `opf` (the default) for core, or the name of another tool such as `pptx.dev/review`.

path.description: JSON Pointer to the value the finding is about, such as `/slides/4/title`. Empty for the whole document, or for a value in a supplied context such as a loaded catalog.

scope.description: `document` (the default) when `path` points into the checked presentation, `context` when it points into host-supplied context such as loaded catalog records.

message.description: What is wrong, in a sentence.

slide.description: Zero-based index of the slide the finding belongs to.

slideId.description: The id of that slide, when it has one.

definition.description: A link to the rule's documentation or to the schema constraint or catalog record the finding is about.

lookup.description: Arguments for the `opf schema` or `opf catalog` command that shows the definition, as an argument list rather than a shell string.

measured.description: The numbers behind the finding, such as `{ "ratio": 2.1, "needed": 4.5 }`.
